subject: math
title: Percents: Percent of a Number and Finding the Whole
seo_title: Grade 6 Percent Worksheets: Percent of a Number, Percent as a Rate per 100 and Finding the Whole
standard_text: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100 (e.g., 30% of a quantity means 30/100 times the quantity); solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 percent worksheets: read percents on 10 × 10 grids, change percents to fractions and decimals, find 10%, 25%, 50% and 75% of a number, find 30% of 70, and find the whole from a part and a percent with double number lines. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_sub: To find the whole, work up to 100%: if 12 is 25% of a number, 100% is 4 times 25%, so the number is 4 × 12 = 48.
body_html:
Percent means “per 100”

Percent means “out of 100.” 30% is 30 out of 100, or 30100. 100% is the whole. 50% is half.

Percents, fractions and decimals

To change a percent to a decimal, divide by 100: move the point 2 places left.

PercentFractionDecimal
1%11000.01
10%1100.1
20%150.2
25%140.25
50%120.5
75%340.75
100%11

Find a percent of a number

Change the percent to a fraction or decimal, then multiply. Benchmark percents make it quick: 10% means divide by 10, 50% means divide by 2, 25% means divide by 4.

Example

What is 30% of 70?

30% = 30100 = 0.3. 0.3 × 70 = 21. Or: 10% of 70 is 7, so 30% is 3 × 7 = 21.

Answer: 21

Find the whole

When you know a part and its percent, work up to 100%.

Example

12 is 25% of what number?

100% is 4 times 25%. So the whole is 4 × 12 = 48. Check: 25% of 48 = 12.

Answer: 48

Example

18 is 30% of what number?

30% is 3 groups of 10%, so 10% is 18 ÷ 3 = 6. 100% is 10 × 6 = 60.

Answer: 60

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
30% of 70 = 30 × 70 = 2,100Percent means per 100: 0.3 × 70 = 21
25% = 0.025Move the point 2 places: 25% = 0.25
0.5% = 50%0.5% is half of 1%. 50% is half of the whole
12 is 25% of ? → 12 × 0.25 = 3The whole is bigger than the part: 12 × 4 = 48
$60 at 25% off saves $60 − 25 = $35Find 25% of $60 first: $15

faq.q: How do you find the percent of a number in 6th grade?
faq.a: Write the percent as a fraction over 100 or as a decimal, then multiply. For example, 30% of 70 = 30/100 × 70 = 0.3 × 70 = 21.
The word comes from “per centum,” Latin for “for each hundred.” So 45% is 45 out of every 100, or 45/100 = 0.45.

faq.q: How do you find the whole when you know the part and the percent?
faq.a: Work up to 100%. If 12 is 25% of a number, then 100% is 4 times 25%, so the whole is 4 × 12 = 48.

faq.q: What is a double number line for percents?
faq.a: It is two number lines that line up: percents on top and amounts below, with 100% matching the whole. It helps students see that 10% of 70 is 7, 30% is 21 and 100% is 70.

sets.title: Percent means per 100: grids, fractions and decimals

items.q: What percent of the grid is shaded?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, and 37 of them are shaded. 37 out of 100 = 37100 = 37%. Percent means “per 100.” (63% is the white part.)

items.q: What percent of the grid is shaded?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, and 8 of them are shaded. 8 out of 100 = 8100 = 8%. Percent means “per 100.” There is no full column, so it is less than 10%. (92% is the white part.)

items.q: What percent of the grid is shaded?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, and 60 of them are shaded. 60 out of 100 = 60100 = 60%. Percent means “per 100.” 6 full columns are 60 squares, not 6%. (40% is the white part.)

items.q: What percent of the grid is shaded?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, and 45 of them are shaded. 45 out of 100 = 45100 = 45%. Percent means “per 100.” (55% is the white part.)

items.q: What percent of the grid is shaded?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, and 92 of them are shaded. 92 out of 100 = 92100 = 92%. Percent means “per 100.” (8% is the white part.)

items.q: What percent of the grid is shaded?
items.e: The grid has 100 equal squares, and 3 of them are shaded. 3 out of 100 = 3100 = 3%. Percent means “per 100.” There is no full column, so it is less than 10%. (97% is the white part.)

items.q: Which fraction in simplest form names the shaded part?
items.e: 25 out of 100 squares are shaded: 25100. Divide the top and bottom by 25: 25100 = 14. It is not 125: 25% means 25 out of 100, not 1 out of 25.

items.q: Which fraction in simplest form names the shaded part?
items.e: 40 out of 100 squares are shaded: 40100. Divide the top and bottom by 20: 40100 = 25. 4100 would be only 4 squares.
Percent means “per 100,” so divide by 100: 25% = 25100 = 0.25. Move the decimal point 2 places left. 0.025 would be 2.5%.
Percent means “per 100,” so divide by 100: 7% = 7100 = 0.07. Move the decimal point 2 places left. 0.7 would be 70%. Write a 0 in the tenths place: 7 hundredths.
Percent means “per 100,” so divide by 100: 60% = 60100 = 0.6. Move the decimal point 2 places left. 0.06 would be only 6%.
Percent means “per 100,” so divide by 100: 125% = 125100 = 1.25. Move the decimal point 2 places left. More than 100% is more than 1 whole, so the decimal is more than 1.
Multiply by 100 (move the point 2 places right): 0.4 = 40100 = 40%. 4% would be 0.04.
Multiply by 100 (move the point 2 places right): 0.05 = 5100 = 5%. 50% would be 0.5.
Multiply by 100 (move the point 2 places right): 0.5 = 50100 = 50%. 0.5% is less than 1%, so it is much smaller than 0.5.

items.q: Write 34 as a percent.
items.e: Make the bottom 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 25: 34 = 75100 = 75%. Do not just write the digits 3 and 4 together.

items.q: Write 15 as a percent.
items.e: Make the bottom 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 20: 15 = 20100 = 20%. Do not write the digits 1 and 5 together. 5% would be 120.

items.q: Write 325 as a percent.
items.e: Make the bottom 100. Multiply the top and bottom by 4: 325 = 12100 = 12%. 3% would be 3100, not 325.

items.q: Which fraction in simplest form is equal to 50%?
items.e: 50% = 50100. Divide the top and bottom by 50: 12. It is not 150: that is 2%.

items.q: Which fraction in simplest form is equal to 20%?
items.e: 20% = 20100. Divide the top and bottom by 20: 15. It is not 120: that is 5%. And 45 is 80%.
10% = 110, so divide by 10: 80 ÷ 10 = 8. Not 10 × 80: percent means per 100.
10% = 110, so divide by 10: 350 ÷ 10 = 35. 3.5 would be 1%.
50% = 12, so divide by 2: 64 ÷ 2 = 32. Half of the number. Do not add or subtract 50.
50% = 12, so divide by 2: 90 ÷ 2 = 45. Half of the number. 180 doubles the number; 50% halves it.
25% = 14, so divide by 4: 80 ÷ 4 = 20. Not 80 ÷ 25: 25% is one fourth. 60 is the other 75%.
25% = 14, so divide by 4: 36 ÷ 4 = 9. 27 is the other 75%, and 18 is 50%.
75% = 34. First find 25%: 80 ÷ 4 = 20. Then 75% is 3 times that: 3 × 20 = 60. 20 is only 25%. Remember to multiply by 3.
75% = 34. First find 25%: 40 ÷ 4 = 10. Then 75% is 3 times that: 3 × 10 = 30. 10 is only 25%.
1% = 1100, so divide by 100: 600 ÷ 100 = 6. 60 would be 10%.
1% = 1100, so divide by 100: 2,500 ÷ 100 = 25. 250 would be 10%.
20% = 15, so divide by 5: 45 ÷ 5 = 9. (Or: 10% is 4.5, and 20% is 2 × 4.5.) Not 45 ÷ 20: 20% is one fifth. 4.5 is only 10%.
20% = 15, so divide by 5: 150 ÷ 5 = 30. (Or: 10% is 15, and 20% is 2 × 15.) 15 is only 10%. 120 is the other 80%.
100% is the whole number, so 200% is 2 times it: 2 × 15 = 30. 200% is more than the whole, so the answer is more than 15.
150% = 100% + 50%. 100% of 40 is 40, and 50% is 20. 40 + 20 = 60. 150% is more than 100%, so the answer is more than 40.

items.q: The double number line shows that 100% is 120. What is 30% of 120?
items.e: 100% matches 120. The lines have 10 equal parts, so each part is 10% and 120 ÷ 10 = 12. 30% is 3 parts: 3 × 12 = 36. The answer is an amount, not the percent 30.

items.q: The double number line shows that 100% is 60. What is 75% of 60?
items.e: 100% matches 60. The lines have 4 equal parts, so each part is 25% and 60 ÷ 4 = 15. 75% is 3 parts: 3 × 15 = 45. The answer is an amount, not the percent 75.

items.q: The double number line shows that 100% is 200. What is 40% of 200?
items.e: 100% matches 200. The lines have 5 equal parts, so each part is 20% and 200 ÷ 5 = 40. 40% is 2 parts: 2 × 40 = 80. The answer is an amount, not the percent 40.

items.q: The double number line shows that 100% is 50. What is 70% of 50?
items.e: 100% matches 50. The lines have 10 equal parts, so each part is 10% and 50 ÷ 10 = 5. 70% is 7 parts: 7 × 5 = 35. The answer is an amount, not the percent 70.

sets.title: Find the percent of a quantity

items.e: 30% = 30100 = 0.3. Multiply: 0.3 × 70 = 21. Check: 10% of 70 is 7, and 3 × 7 = 21. Not 30 × 70: percent means per 100.
15% = 15100 = 0.15. Multiply: 0.15 × 60 = 9. Check: 10% of 60 is 6 and 5% is 3, so 15% is 9. Not 60 ÷ 15 = 4. 51 is the other 85%.
40% = 40100 = 0.4. Multiply: 0.4 × 85 = 34. 8.5 is only 10%.
35% = 35100 = 0.35. Multiply: 0.35 × 80 = 28. Check: 10% of 80 is 8 and 5% is 4, so 35% is 28. Do not add the percent to the number.
12% = 12100 = 0.12. Multiply: 0.12 × 50 = 6. 44 is the other 88%.
8% = 8100 = 0.08. Multiply: 0.08 × 25 = 2. 8% = 0.08, not 0.8.
65% = 65100 = 0.65. Multiply: 0.65 × 40 = 26. Check: 10% of 40 is 4 and 5% is 2, so 65% is 26. 14 is the other 35%.
45% = 45100 = 0.45. Multiply: 0.45 × 120 = 54. Check: 10% of 120 is 12 and 5% is 6, so 45% is 54. 66 is the other 55%.
90% = 90100 = 0.9. Multiply: 0.9 × 30 = 27. Check: 10% of 30 is 3, and 9 × 3 = 27. 3 is only 10%. 90% is almost all of 30.
6% = 6100 = 0.06. Multiply: 0.06 × 150 = 9. 6% = 0.06, not 0.6. And not 150 ÷ 6.
18% = 18100 = 0.18. Multiply: 0.18 × 200 = 36. 18% of 200 is 2 × 18, because 1% of 200 is 2.
2% = 2100 = 0.02. Multiply: 0.02 × 450 = 9. 2% = 0.02, not 0.2. And not 450 ÷ 2.
30% = 30100 = 0.3. Multiply: 0.3 × 15 = 4.5. Check the decimal point: 3 × 1.5 = 4.5.
120% = 120100 = 1.2. Multiply: 1.2 × 35 = 42. 120% is more than 100%, so the answer is more than 35.
0.5% = 0.5100 = 0.005. Multiply: 0.005 × 400 = 2. 0.5% is half of 1%, not 50%. 1% of 400 is 4, so 0.5% is 2.
125% = 125100 = 1.25. Multiply: 1.25 × 48 = 60. 125% = 100% + 25% = 48 + 12.
3% = 3100 = 0.03. Multiply: 0.03 × 1,200 = 36. 3% = 0.03, not 0.3. And not 1,200 ÷ 3.
24% = 24100 = 0.24. Multiply: 0.24 × 75 = 18. 57 is the other 76%.
30% means 30 per 100, so 30% of 70 is 30100 × 70 = 21. 30 × 70 forgets to divide by 100.
15% = 15100 = 0.15, so 15% of 60 is 0.15 × 60 = 9. 0.015 would be 1.5%.

sets.title: Find the whole from a part and a percent

items.q: 12 is 25% of a number. What is the number?
items.e: 12 is 25% of the whole. 100% is 4 times 25%, so the whole is 4 × 12 = 48. Check: 25% of 48 is 12. Do not multiply 12 by 25%: that finds a part of 12, not the whole.

items.q: 30 is 75% of a number. What is the number?
items.e: 75% is 3 groups of 25%. So 25% is 30 ÷ 3 = 10. 100% is 4 groups of 25%: 4 × 10 = 40. Check: 75% of 40 is 30. Do not multiply 30 by 75%: that finds a part of 30, not the whole.

items.q: 18 is 30% of a number. What is the number?
items.e: 30% is 3 groups of 10%. So 10% is 18 ÷ 3 = 6. 100% is 10 groups of 10%: 10 × 6 = 60. Check: 30% of 60 is 18. Do not multiply 18 by 30%: that finds a part of 18, not the whole.

items.q: 24 is 80% of a number. What is the number?
items.e: 80% is 4 groups of 20%. So 20% is 24 ÷ 4 = 6. 100% is 5 groups of 20%: 5 × 6 = 30. Check: 80% of 30 is 24. Do not multiply 24 by 80%: that finds a part of 24, not the whole.
9 is 10% of the whole. 100% is 10 times 10%, so the whole is 10 × 9 = 90. Check: 10% of 90 is 9. The whole is bigger than the part.
15 is 50% of the whole. 100% is 2 times 50%, so the whole is 2 × 15 = 30. Check: 50% of 30 is 15. 50% is half, so the whole is double.
7 is 20% of the whole. 100% is 5 times 20%, so the whole is 5 × 7 = 35. Check: 20% of 35 is 7. 28 is the other 80%.
6 is 5% of the whole. 100% is 20 times 5%, so the whole is 20 × 6 = 120. Check: 5% of 120 is 6. 30 would be 6 × 5. The whole is 20 times 5%.
4 is 1% of the whole. 100% is 100 times 1%, so the whole is 100 × 4 = 400. Check: 1% of 400 is 4. 1% is a very small part, so the whole is much bigger than 4.
35% is 7 groups of 5%. So 5% is 21 ÷ 7 = 3. 100% is 20 groups of 5%: 20 × 3 = 60. Check: 35% of 60 is 21. 39 is the other 65%.
90% is 9 groups of 10%. So 10% is 45 ÷ 9 = 5. 100% is 10 groups of 10%: 10 × 5 = 50. Check: 90% of 50 is 45. 90% is almost all, so the whole is a little more than 45.
40% is 2 groups of 20%. So 20% is 16 ÷ 2 = 8. 100% is 5 groups of 20%: 5 × 8 = 40. Check: 40% of 40 is 16. 24 is the other 60%.
45% is 9 groups of 5%. So 5% is 27 ÷ 9 = 3. 100% is 20 groups of 5%: 20 × 3 = 60. Check: 45% of 60 is 27. 33 is the other 55%.
120% is 6 groups of 20%. So 20% is 36 ÷ 6 = 6. 100% is 5 groups of 20%: 5 × 6 = 30. Check: 120% of 30 is 36. 120% is more than the whole, so the whole is less than 36.
12% is 3 groups of 4%. So 4% is 3 ÷ 3 = 1. 100% is 25 groups of 4%: 25 × 1 = 25. Check: 12% of 25 is 3. 22 is the other 88%.
65% is 13 groups of 5%. So 5% is 13 ÷ 13 = 1. 100% is 20 groups of 5%: 20 × 1 = 20. Check: 65% of 20 is 13. 7 is the other 35%.
Write the part over the whole and make the bottom 100: 920 = 45100 = 45%. The part is 9, but the percent is out of 100.
Write the part over the whole and make the bottom 100: 624 = 14 = 25100 = 25%. The part is 6, but the percent is out of 100.
Write the part over the whole and make the bottom 100: 1440 = 720 = 35100 = 35%. The part is 14, but the percent is out of 100.
Write the part over the whole and make the bottom 100: 33300 = 11100 = 11%. The part is 33, but the percent is out of 100.

sets.title: Percent word problems: tests, discounts, surveys and sports

items.q: Maya got 18 out of 20 questions right on a quiz. What percent did she get right?
items.e: 1820 = 90100 = 90%. Multiply the top and bottom by 5 to get a bottom of 100. (10% is the part she got wrong.)

items.q: A test has 40 questions. Sam scored 85%. How many questions did he get right?
items.e: 85% of 40 = 0.85 × 40 = 34. Check: 10% of 40 is 4, so 5% is 2 and 85% is 8 × 4 + 2 = 34. (6 is the number he got wrong.)

items.q: A spelling test has 25 words. Each word is worth the same. What percent is each word worth?
items.e: The whole test is 100%. Share 100% among 25 words: 100 ÷ 25 = 4%. So 125 = 4100.

items.q: Jack buys a $60 jacket that is 25% off. How much money does he save?
items.e: 25% = 14, so the discount is $60 ÷ 4 = $15. $45 is the sale price, not the amount saved. Do not subtract 25 from 60.

items.q: Shoes cost $80. They are 15% off. How many dollars off is that?
items.e: 15% of $80 = 0.15 × 80 = $12. Check: 10% is $8 and 5% is $4, so 15% is $12. ($68 is the new price.)

items.q: A video game costs $45. It is on sale for 20% off. How much is the discount?
items.e: 20% = 15, so the discount is $45 ÷ 5 = $9. Not $45 ÷ 20: 20% means 20 per 100.

items.q: A store takes $6 off the price of a lamp. That is 10% off. What was the price of the lamp?
items.e: $6 is 10% of the price. 100% is 10 times 10%: 10 × $6 = $60. Check: 10% of $60 is $6.

items.q: In a class of 25 students, 40% walk to school. How many students walk?
items.e: 40% of 25 = 0.4 × 25 = 10. Check: 20% of 25 is 5, so 40% is 10. (15 students do not walk.)

items.q: In a class survey, 12 students chose pizza. That is 30% of the class. How many students are in the class?
items.e: 30% is 3 groups of 10%, so 10% is 12 ÷ 3 = 4. 100% is 10 × 4 = 40 students. Check: 30% of 40 is 12. 3.6 is 30% of 12, which finds a part, not the whole.

items.q: A school has 500 students. 8% of them are left-handed. How many students are left-handed?
Emma took 15 free throws in a basketball game and made 60% of them. How many free throws did she make?
items.e: 60% of 15 = 0.6 × 15 = 9. Check: 10% of 15 is 1.5, and 6 × 1.5 = 9. (6 is the number she missed.)

items.q: A soccer team won 75% of its games this season. It won 18 games. How many games did the team play?
items.e: 75% is 3 groups of 25%, so 25% is 18 ÷ 3 = 6. 100% is 4 × 6 = 24 games. Check: 75% of 24 is 18.

items.q: Grace took 16 shots in a hockey game and scored on 4 of them. What percent of her shots scored?
items.e: 416 = 14 = 25100 = 25%. (75% of the shots did not score.)

items.q: A 2-liter water bottle holds 2,000 mL. It is 35% full. How many milliliters of water are in it?
Owen has saved $45 for a bike. That is 30% of the price. What is the price of the bike?
items.e: 30% is 3 groups of 10%, so 10% is $45 ÷ 3 = $15. 100% is 10 × $15 = $150. Check: 30% of $150 is $45. ($105 is the money he still needs.)

items.q: A file is 40% downloaded. So far, 120 MB have downloaded. How big is the whole file?
A school bus is 75% full. There are 36 students on it. How many seats does the bus have?
items.e: 75% is 3 groups of 25%, so 25% is 36 ÷ 3 = 12 seats. 100% is 4 × 12 = 48 seats. (12 seats are empty.)

items.q: Which is more: 30% of 50 or 50% of 30?
items.e: 30% of 50 = 0.3 × 50 = 15. 50% of 30 = half of 30 = 15. They are equal. (Both are 30 × 50 ÷ 100.)

items.q: Ben got 17 out of 20 on a math test. Ava got 42 out of 50 on another test. Who got the higher percent?
items.e: Ben: 1720 = 85100 = 85%. Ava: 4250 = 84100 = 84%. 85% > 84%, so Ben got the higher percent, even though Ava got more points.

items.q: A book has 220 pages. Zoe has read 45% of it. How many pages has she read?
items.e: 45% of 220 = 0.45 × 220 = 99 pages. Check: 10% is 22 and 5% is 11, so 45% is 4 × 22 + 11 = 99. (121 pages are left to read.)
